title: What does a second speaker add?
hook: Two speakers play the same note. Walk along in front of them: what do you hear?

doesNotKnow: that a half-wavelength path difference makes waves cancel

misconception: Two sounds are always louder than one.
objective: The learner can explain that waves add by height, so where one path is half a wavelength longer, crest meets trough and the sound cancels.

claims.source: Principle of superposition for linear waves; Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 16-17.

claims.text: With equal amplitudes, a path difference of half a wavelength makes the waves cancel; zero or one whole wavelength makes them add to twice one speaker's amplitude.
claims.source: A sin(wt) + A sin(wt - 2 pi D / lambda) has amplitude |2 A cos(pi D / lambda)|: 2A at D = 0 or lambda, 0 at D = lambda/2; 1.41 A at D = lambda/4.

claims.text: A 343 Hz tone in air has a wavelength of 1.00 m.
claims.source: lambda = v / f = 343 m/s / 343 Hz = 1.00 m (sound speed in dry air at 20 C).

claims.text: With speakers 1.5 m apart and the listener 4 m in front, A's path is 0.50 m longer at 1.44 m to the right, and 1.00 m longer at 3.61 m.
Idealised: each speaker is taken as equally loud at the listener, with no echoes; in a real room the cancelled spot is quiet, not silent.
claims.source: Stated on stage and in the reveal. With 1/r spreading the paths at x = 1.44 m (4.56 vs 4.06 m) give amplitudes in ratio 0.89, leaving about 12% of one speaker's amplitude; reflections also fill in the minimum.

claims.text: A wavelength is the length of one full wave; for this 343 Hz tone in air it is 1.00 m.
claims.source: Definition of wavelength; 343 m/s divided by 343 Hz = 1.00 m (see c3). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): 343 m/s / 343 Hz = 1.00 m; LAMBDA in Demo.tsx line 24.

recall.question: Noise-cancelling headphones play a sound into your ear. To cancel a hum, that sound must be…
options: The same hum, shifted half a cycle
recall.why: Waves add by height: a copy shifted half a cycle puts its crests on the hum's troughs, and they cancel.
